key_insight: In this LLM-assisted systematic review case study, most evidence-processing errors were traceable, correctable, and sometimes changed pooled findings, showing that downstream review outputs depend heavily on how source judgments are operationalized.
clinical_relevance: For clinical evidence synthesis, the study highlights that transparent rules for cohort overlap, outcome coding, and correction workflows can reduce the risk of misleading review conclusions.
method: Retrospective, non-blinded methodological case study of one registered prognostic review.
Reconciled frozen correction and audit records into distinct root-cause events.
Tracked each error’s impact on analysis membership, weighting, pooled results, certainty, and publication files.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 50 root-cause events, 12 of which changed pooled results before correction, across a review of 454 reports and 445 studies.
watch_item: This is a single internal case study with no external comparator, so it cannot estimate general error rates or prove that the workflow will perform similarly in other reviews.
paper_title: Evidence-processing errors and their correction in an LLM-assisted systematic review: a retrospective methodological case study
